Let me do a lookup for the email and name. I can make two independent lookups in one block:
- register_lookup with "timo.kuenzig@example.de"
- register_lookup with "Künzig" (to see family and check Milla isn't already registered)

Then, based on results:
- Add Milla Künzig to the register: email sabine.kuenzig@example.de (mother's contact email — likely the contact), first_name Milla, last_name Künzig, team Kindergarde, birth_year 2016. Fee status: what? Fees: jahresbeitrag 60.0, gardemitglied 30.0. The Geschwisterbeitrag (sibling discount) — there's no explicit sibling fee listed in the club facts. The club facts say: "if a fee is not listed, say you will confirm". So I must NOT invent a Geschwisterbeitrag amount. Timo is already a member; the mother asks about a sibling discount. Since no Geschwisterbeitrag is listed in the fees, I should say we will confirm it.

For Milla as Kindergarde member, gardemitglied fee is 30.0. That's the gardemitglied fee — presumably applies to Garden members. So Milla would pay the Gardemitglied fee of 30 €. The Geschwisterbeitrag is not listed, so I'll confirm.

Wait — should the fee be gardemitglied 30.0 for her? The fees list has "gardemitglied: 30.0" which seems to be the fee for Garden members (active guards). Kindergarde is a Garde, so 30 € Gardemitglied fee seems right. I can state that the Gardemitglied-Beitrag is 30 €. But the Geschwister discount question — not listed, so confirm.

Fee status for new member: default "invoice_sent"? Maybe better "trial" since she's new and just joining? The proposed action says "Standard-Anmeldeprozess für die Kindergarde einleiten". I'd set fee_status to "invoice_sent" (default) or maybe leave default. Hmm, but if the Geschwisterbeitrag is unconfirmed, sending an invoice might be premature. Perhaps set fee_status to "open" or "trial"? The tool default is invoice_sent. Given uncertainty, maybe "trial" is safer — she's newly joining. Actually, "Standard-Anmeldeprozess" — I'll set fee_status to "open"... but allowed values mentioned: 'invoice_sent', 'paid', 'trial'. I'll use "trial"? Hmm, she's not on trial, she wants to join. Actually a Kindergarde beginner — "trial" could fit (Garde training usually starts with trial sessions). But she said "möchte unbedingt zur Kindergarde" and asked what to do — she hasn't started yet. The standard process: register, invoice. But since the fee amount might change due to sibling discount, invoicing now could be wrong.

I think setting fee_status to "trial" is reasonable... but it might misrepresent. Alternatively "invoice_sent" with notes that Geschwisterbeitrag needs confirmation. Hmm. The rules say never invent fees. Adding her with default invoice_sent doesn't invent a fee per se, but it implies an invoice was sent. Let me set fee_status to "trial" with a note? Actually, let me think about what's most sensible operationally: The secretary will confirm the Geschwisterbeitrag, then invoice. So the member's current fee status is pending/open. Among allowed values, "trial" seems closest to "not yet invoiced, in onboarding". Hmm, but "trial" implies Probe Training.

Alternatively I could pass fee_status "open" — the schema just says fee_status type string, e.g. those values. I could use "open" as a valid string. The examples say "e.g.", so other values may be fine. I'll use "open" — meaning fee clarification pending. Hmm, risk: demo sandbox may expect specific values. "e.g." implies not exhaustive. I'll go with "open" and note "Geschwisterbeitrag zu klären" in notes.

Hmm, actually, let me reconsider: Simpler to use default invoice_sent? No — an invoice hasn't been sent and amount is unclear. "open" is honest. I'll do that.

Also: notes: "Geschwister von Timo Künzig (timo.kuenzig@example.de); Geschwisterbeitrag bitte klären." Joined: today (default empty = today). Email: mother's email sabine.kuenzig@example.de as contact.

3. Draft reply to sabine.kuenzig@example.de:
- Warm, rheinisch-jovial, concise German, max ~120 words.
- Welcome Milla to Kindergarde.
- Explain: registered, next steps (maybe training times — don't invent specifics; keep general: "Die Trainingszeiten schicken wir euch zu" — careful not to invent. I can say we'll send details).
- Fee: Gardemitglied-Beitrag 30 € per... presumably per season/Jahr? The facts list fees without period. I should be careful: "Der Beitrag für Gardemitglieder beträgt 30 €." Period not specified — avoid inventing "pro Jahr"? Jahresbeitrag is clearly yearly. Gardemitglied fee period is ambiguous. Safer: "der Beitrag für die Garde beträgt 30 €" without period, or confirm. Hmm. The jahresbeitrag 60 and gardemitglied 30 — gardemitglied likely replaces/relates to annual fee for guard members. I'll phrase: "Als Gardemitglied fällt für Milla ein Beitrag von 30 € an" — no period. That states only the listed fact.
- Geschwisterbeitrag: not in the listed facts → say we will confirm. "Ob und wie der Geschwisterbeitrag ausfällt, klären wir kurz und melden uns" — good.
- Signature exactly as configured:
Der Elferrat
KG Rheinklause 1967 e.V.
(Entwurf erstellt von ClubSteward, dem Vereins-Agenten — vom Menschen freigegeben)

Order: lookups first (dependent decisions follow). Then add + draft can be parallel? The add doesn't depend on draft content, and draft doesn't depend on add result — but ideally confirm add success before telling them registered. To be safe, do lookups first in one block; then add + save_draft in one block (draft doesn't depend on add's output value); then log_activity last (depends on outcomes). Actually save_draft and register_add are independent of each other. Then log after seeing results.
